hint.afterNumber: after «{word}»: {cat, select, one {one, the singular} two {two, the dual} few {three and four, the plural} other {five and up, the genitive plural}}
hint.ruleAdverb: How something is done: the adverb, most often in -o, not the adjective.
hint.ruleAgree: An adjective (and my, your, our …) takes its noun's gender and number: masculine, feminine or neuter.
hint.ruleAspect: Going on, or again and again (Kaj delam?): the imperfective. Done once, to the end (Kaj naredim?): the perfective.
hint.ruleBiti: Biti (to be) takes the person who is: one form for one, another for several.
hint.ruleCases: Six cases, each with its question: 1 kdo? kaj? 2 koga? česa? 3 komu? čemu? 4 koga? kaj? 5 pri kom? o čem? 6 s kom? s čim?
hint.ruleClitics: The short words go second in the sentence, in a fixed order: biti's forms, se, to whom, whom, je.
hint.ruleComparative: Comparing: -ši, -ejši or bolj … (lepši, starejši); the most: naj- (najlepši).
hint.ruleDual: Exactly two people or things: the dual, with its own endings (-va, -ta).
hint.ruleFuture: The future: biti's future form and the l-form (-l, -la, -li).
hint.ruleGender: Every noun has a gender: a consonant at the end is mostly masculine, -a feminine, -o and -e neuter. Pronouns and adjectives follow it.
hint.ruleImperative: Telling someone to do it: the imperative, its ending by whom you tell: one (ti), several or politely (vi), two, or us two.
hint.ruleJoining: Joining words: because, so, although, but, when: each joins two sentences its own way.
hint.ruleKi: Who, which, that: ki, the same for all; a short pronoun after it says the case.
hint.ruleModal: After must, may, want to, know how to: the infinitive (-ti); lahko keeps the verb's person.
hint.ruleNoTwice: Slovene says no twice: ne with nič, nihče, nikoli.
hint.ruleNumberAgrees: The number agrees with its noun's gender: en, ena, eno; dva, dve; trije, tri; štirje, štiri.
hint.ruleNumbers: The noun after a number: 1 the singular, 2 the dual, 3 and 4 the plural, 5 and up the genitive plural.
hint.ruleOrdinal: Which one in a row: the ordinal, which agrees like an adjective; a date takes the genitive.
hint.rulePast: The past: biti in the present and the l-form (-l, -la, -li), which takes the doer's gender.
hint.rulePerson: The verb's ending says who does it: -m I, -š you, no ending he or she, -va we two, -mo we, -te you all, -jo they.
hint.rulePlural: Three or more take the plural: masculine -i, feminine -e, neuter -a; two take the dual.
hint.rulePronouns: A personal pronoun has a long form (for emphasis and after a preposition) and a short one (otherwise); one for one person or thing, another for several.
hint.ruleQuestions: Question words: kje? where (a place), kam? where to, od kod? where from, kdaj? when, zakaj? why, koliko? how many.
hint.ruleReflexive: Some verbs come with se, which goes second in the sentence; to be afraid (bati se) takes the genitive.
hint.ruleReported: Reported speech: da for a statement, naj for a wish or an order, ali for a question; the tense stays as it was said.
hint.ruleSupine: After a verb of going (to go, to come): the supine, the infinitive without its -i.
hint.ruleSvoj: What belongs to the one who does it (the subject) takes the reflexive possessive, whoever it is.
hint.ruleTiVi: Who are you talking to? Someone older, a stranger, in a shop: vi (the verb in -te). A friend, a child, family: ti.
hint.ruleWhen: When: ob + the locative for an hour (ob devetih); ob pol + the next hour in the genitive (ob pol devetih); v + the accusative for a day (v soboto); čez (in) + the accusative, pred (ago) + the instrumental; a part of the day or a season is one word (zvečer, jeseni).
hint.ruleWhere: Where something is: v, na, ob, pri take the locative; pod, nad, pred, za, med the instrumental.
hint.ruleWhereTo: Where something goes: v, na, pod, za … take the accusative; k, h the dative.
hint.ruleWould: Would: bi and the l-form; I'd like is rad bi (a woman: rada bi).
hint.ruleStems: Some nouns grow their stem in the other cases (a -t-, -n-, -er- or -ev- added, or an e that drops); the endings after it are the usual ones.
hint.ruleDualCases: Two in a case: the dual's own endings, -ov, -oma, -ih for a masculine noun, -ama, -ah for a feminine one; the word for two declines too.
hint.ruleAspectTenses: Aspect in every tense: done once, to the end, the perfective; going on, again and again, or telling someone not to, the imperfective.
hint.ruleDefinite: Which one? One already known or picked out takes the definite form in -i; a new one, or after biti, the plain form.
hint.ruleClauses: A clause joins the sentence with a word that says how: the cause, a condition, an aim (with the l-form), what came of it, although; after a clause in front come the short words.
hint.ruleTimeNoPrep: A time without a preposition: the genitive for a date or a day told of (the fifth of May, one day, in 1918), the accusative for this, next, every and how long.
hint.ruleFeelings: How you feel: who feels it is in the dative with cold, sorry, bored, in a hurry, and in the accusative with it hurts, I'm freezing, I'm afraid.
hint.rulePluralCases: The plural has its own ending in each case: masculine -ov in the genitive, -om in the dative, -ih in the locative, -i in the instrumental; feminine and neuter nouns have no ending in the genitive.
hint.ruleWhose: A possessive agrees with what is owned, like an adjective: -ov or -ev for a man, -in for a woman.
hint.ruleNumberVerb: The verb after a number: one, the singular; two, the dual; three and four, the plural; from five, and after a lot, a little, some: the singular, neuter (-lo in the past).
hint.ruleIfWould: Imagined, unlikely or past: bi and the l-form in both halves. A real chance: the future in both.
hint.ruleCliticOrder: The short words go second in the sentence, in a fixed order: biti's forms, se, to whom, whom, then je; after a no, the no comes first.
hint.ruleVerbalNoun: A verbal noun names the doing: -ati becomes -anje, -iti -enje, a verb with a -t form -tje; it is neuter, and what is done follows in the genitive.
hint.ruleIndefinite: Some-, no-, every-: ne- for some (someone, something), ni- for no (nobody, nothing), vsak- or vse for every; a no-word keeps the no before the verb.
hint.rulePassive: The passive: biti and the form in -n or -t for how something is after it was done, agreeing like an adjective; se for what is done in general.
hint.ruleCompareFull: Comparing in full: as … as (tako … kot), much more (veliko and the comparative), as … as possible (čim and the comparative), the more …, the more … (bolj ko …, bolj …), too (pre-).
hint.rulePluperfect: Before the past: biti in the past (sem bil, je bila) and the l-form, both agreeing, for what had happened first; in speech, the past with že.
hint.ruleClausesMore: More joining words: although (kljub temu da), while (medtem ko), after (potem ko), until (dokler ne), as soon as (takoj ko), unless (razen če); with bi: without (ne da bi), instead of (namesto da bi), as if (kot da bi).
hint.ruleIdioms: An idiom means more than its words: learn it whole. Only the verb changes, and the person's case (to whom: the dative; whom: the accusative).
hint.ruleNumberWords: More number words: how many times (-krat; the first time, prvič), what kind (dvojen, trojen), how many of a plural-only noun (dvoje, troje), a number as a noun (-ica); after a preposition the number declines.
hint.ruleGerund: How it is done, at the same time: the form in -e or -aje (silently, standing, crying), in books also -eč or -oč; it never changes, and its doer is the main verb's subject.
hint.ruleDiminutive: A little one: -ica or -ka for a feminine noun, -ek or -ček for a masculine one, -ce or -ece for a neuter one; it keeps its gender and declines by its own ending.
hint.ruleCommands: Commands: let's (-va for two of us, -mo for more), let him or them (naj and the present), don't (ne and the imperfective; ne and the perfective to warn of a slip); politely, bi … lahko.
hint.ruleParticiple: A participle as an adjective: -n or -t for what was done to it, -l for what it became, -eč or -oč for what goes on; it agrees like an adjective.
hint.ruleWordFamily: A word family: who does it (-ar, -ec, -telj), a woman (-ka, -ica), where (-arna, -nica, -išče), what it is like (-ost, -ota).
hint.rulePrefix: A prefix makes the verb perfective (done once, to the end) and may change its meaning; for what goes on or comes again, the new imperfective in -ovati or -ati.
hint.ruleTwoCases: One preposition, two cases, two meanings: the accusative for where to and what you go for (or how long), the locative or the instrumental for where.
hint.ruleSpoken: Spoken and written are both right in their place: spoken at home and with friends, the standard in writing. Understand the spoken form, write the standard one.
hint.ruleFormalLetter: A formal letter: Spoštovani or Spoštovana and a comma, then a small letter; Vi with a capital and the verb in the plural, the l-form masculine plural; close with S spoštovanjem.
hint.rulePastConditional: What would have been, and wasn't: bil bi and the l-form, both agreeing with the doer; in speech often just bi with a word of the past.
hint.ruleImpersonal: No one as the subject: treba je and the infinitive, se for people in general, the weather on its own; in the past, the neuter singular (-lo).
hint.ruleWhichWhose: Who, which, whose: kateri takes the case of its own clause, čigar is whose for a man, kdor whoever, kar what, or which for a whole sentence.
hint.ruleWordOrder: Word order: what is known comes first, the news last; the short words second; a contrast first, with pa after it; tudi and samo right before their word.
hint.withNoun: with the noun «{word}»: by its gender
hint.en.ruleAdverbs: A thing: a slow walk; what is done: Jack walks slowly. Spelling: carefully, happily, gently. On their own: well; fast, hard don't change. After the object: Sam plays darts well.
hint.en.ruleArticles: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound: a horse, an apple, an hour, a uniform. the for what's known, or the only one: the sun, the pond. They never change.
hint.en.ruleAskedWhere: asked where + a statement's order: He asked where I lived. Yes or no: asked if, asked whether: She asked if I wanted tea. The tense one step back. Polite: Do you know where the inn is? Could you tell me where the bus stops?
hint.en.ruleBe: I am, he / she / it is, you / we / they are; short with an apostrophe, joined to the word before it. The negative adds not: is not, are not. A question starts with the verb: Are you ready? be needs no do, does or don't.
hint.en.ruleCan: can + the verb, the same for everyone: I can swim. She can swim (never cans, never to swim). Negative can't; question Can you swim? — Yes, I can. Past could.
hint.en.ruleCollocations: make: a decision, a mistake, a noise. do: the washing up, your best, a favour. take: a photo, a seat, the bus. have: a chat, a rest, lunch. heavy rain, strong tea, thick fog. An idiom: a piece of cake.
hint.en.ruleCompare: Short: older than, the oldest; long: more useful than, the most useful. Spelling: bigger, nicer, happier. On their own: better, the best; worse, the worst; further, the furthest.
hint.en.ruleContrast: + a sentence: although, even though, because, so that. + a noun or -ing: despite, in spite of, because of. A new sentence: However, … As a result, … What for: to, in order to + the base form.
hint.en.ruleDo: With most verbs a question and a negative need do / does, the verb unchanged: Do you live here? Does she live here? I do not live here (not alone: I not live). She does not live here. Past: did, did not.
hint.en.ruleEmphasis: It was + a person + who; a thing, place, time + that: It was Jack who found her. What + a clause + is: What I need is a rest. What Jack did was ring the inn. did + the base form: She did ring. To recognise: Never have I seen …
hint.en.ruleForSince: Still going on: have, has + the participle. for + how long: for ten years. since + when it began: since 2016. To ask: How long have you lived here? Over: the past simple, I lived in Leeds for five years.
hint.en.ruleFormal: Dear Sir or Madam, … Yours faithfully, Dear Mrs Birkett, … Yours sincerely, Formal, whole forms: I am writing to, I would be grateful. To a friend: Hi Jack, Thanks, Cheers. To understand: gonna, gotta, innit. lift, American elevator.
hint.en.ruleFuture: going to + the base form: a plan, or what you can see coming: It's going to rain. will, short 'll, + the base form: decided now, an offer, a promise: We'll help you! An arrangement: We're meeting on Saturday. After when and if, the present, no will.
hint.en.ruleGuess: Perhaps: might, may, could: It might rain. Perhaps not: might not, may not. Sure it is: must: That must be Jack. Sure it isn't: can't: It can't be Jack. Likely: He'll probably come. He probably won't come.
hint.en.ruleHabits: Habits and facts: I walk, you walk, we walk, they walk, but he / she / it walks. After s, x, ch, sh, o -es: does, watches; a consonant + y -ies: flies; have → has.
hint.en.ruleHave: For what you own, have or have got: I have a dog. I've got a dog. She has a dog. She's got a dog. Negative don't have, haven't got; question Do you have …? Have you got …?
hint.en.ruleHaveItDone: have + thing + the participle: I had my hair cut. We've had the fence painted. In talk get: I got my hair cut. With a person: I'll get Jack to look at it. Something bad: He had his wallet stolen.
hint.en.ruleIf: Always so: if + the present twice: If you heat butter, it melts. May happen: if + the present, then will: If it rains, I'll stay. when for what will surely happen: When I get home, I'll call you. After if and when, no will.
hint.en.ruleIfHad: What didn't happen: if + had + the participle, then would have + the participle: If I had known, I would have come. Said: If I'd known, I'd have come. The first 'd is had, the second would. Also could have, might have.
hint.en.ruleIfWould: What isn't so: if + the past, then would: If I had a boat, I'd row across. Also could, might. With be were, spoken also was: If I were you, I'd wait. What may happen: If I have time, I'll help.
hint.en.ruleImperatives: The base form, no you: Sit down! No: Don't run! Together: Let's go! Kindly: Come in, please.
hint.en.ruleIndefinite: someone, something, somewhere: yes, offers. anyone, anything, anywhere: no, questions. no one, nothing, nowhere: the verb stays yes. everyone, everything, everywhere: a singular verb.
hint.en.ruleLinking: because: the reason. so: the result. One sentence, one of them: We stayed because it rained. It rained, so we stayed. before, after, when first: a comma.
hint.en.ruleMixedIf: Then, so now: If I'd listened, I'd be there now. Still so, so then: If I knew the way, I wouldn't have got lost. unless: if not. as long as, provided that: only if. in case: because it may happen. For the future, the present, no will.
hint.en.ruleMust: have to, has to, must: you need to. mustn't: not allowed. don't have to: no need. should: advice. All + the base form: Jack has to go. You mustn't smoke. You don't have to pay. You should rest. The past: had to.
hint.en.ruleNow: What's going on right now: be + verb + -ing: I'm walking, she's walking, they're walking. Negative isn't, aren't; question Is she walking?
hint.en.ruleNumbers: 13 to 19 in -teen, the tens in -ty: fifteen, fifty. twenty-one with a hyphen; a hundred and five; from two on, the plural.
hint.en.ruleObjectPronouns: After a verb or a preposition: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Jack knows her. Sit with me. him, never his; It's me.
hint.en.ruleParticipleClauses: Walking up the fell, I saw a raven. A reason: Not knowing the way, we asked. After a noun: the man standing by the gate, a mill built in 1800. One thing first: Having finished, we went home. One subject for both halves.
hint.en.rulePassive: is, are + the participle: The bread is baked here. was, were + the participle: The bridge was built in 1720. Who: by. No did: Was it sent? can be + the participle: It can be opened.
hint.en.rulePassiveMore: has been mended, is being mended, had been cut, will be finished, should have been shut. People say: It is said that the tarn is deep. Old Wilf is said to be ninety. The past: is said to have been built.
hint.en.rulePast: Finished, at a time that is over (yesterday, last week, ago): regular verbs add -ed, the same for everyone: played, cleaned; many have their own: ate, swam, flew. One word, no helper. Questions and the no: did, didn't + the base form (not do, don't). be: was, were.
hint.en.rulePastModals: A modal + have + the participle looks back: You should have told me. (it was right) It must have been Sam. (I'm sure) It can't have been Poppy. (I'm sure not) It might have been the wind. (perhaps) I needn't have run. (no need)
hint.en.rulePastPerfect: have, has reach up to now; what came earlier still: had + the participle, short 'd: When we got there, the bus had gone. We hadn't eaten. By the time we got there, the bus had gone. In order stays the past simple: I got up, fed the dogs and left.
hint.en.rulePatterns: decide, want, hope + to. enjoy, finish, mind + -ing. like, start both. After a small word -ing: good at walking. want, ask, tell + someone + to: I want you to go.
hint.en.rulePerfect: have, has + the past participle joins the past to now: you've flown, she's climbed. For experience (ever, never), and with since and for. One no in writing: we've never flown. A finished time takes the past simple: we flew there yesterday.
hint.en.rulePerfectGoingOn: have, has + been + -ing: what has gone on up to now, I've been waiting for an hour. The time or the result: She's been baking all morning. She's baked forty scones. No -ing: know, own, belong, understand, believe: I've known Jack for years.
hint.en.rulePhrasal: Verb + small word = a new meaning: get up, look after. Only the verb changes: got up. Some stay together: look after them. Others can part: Turn the radio off. A pronoun in between: Turn it off.
hint.en.rulePhrasalMore: Three words stay together: We've run out of milk. look forward to + -ing: I look forward to seeing you. Together too: come across, take after, get over: I came across it. These part: turn down, call off, bring up: They called it off.
hint.en.rulePlace: in inside (in the box, in Leeds), on on top (on the shelf, on the bus), at a place as a point (at the station, at home, at school). The preposition goes before the noun.
hint.en.rulePlurals: Most nouns add -s: dogs; after s, x, ch, sh -es: boxes; a consonant + y -ies: ponies; -f, -fe -ves: knives.
hint.en.rulePossessive: An owner takes 's: Jack's dog, the children's books; a plural in -s just ': the girls' bikes. Before a noun my, your, his, her, its, our, their; alone mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.
hint.en.rulePronouns: Always say the subject: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're. you is one person or many, polite or not; a thing is it.
hint.en.ruleQuantifiers: Two: both, neither, either. Pairs: both … and, neither … nor. More: every sheep, each of them, all of them, none of them. Before a pronoun of: most of them, one of them.
hint.en.ruleReported: say + what, tell + who: She said she was tired. She told me she was tired. One step back: is → was, will → would, can → could, saw → had seen. If it's still so, also She said she's tired. An order: She told me to wait.
hint.en.ruleReporting: promised to come, refused to pay. advised me to wait, warned us not to go. suggested going, admitted taking, denied taking. suggested that we go. apologised for being late.
hint.en.ruleResult: so + an adjective + that: so cold that. such a + a noun + that: such a cold night that. so much rain, so many people. Two facts: whereas, while. A new sentence: Nevertheless, In order: firstly, to sum up. An opinion: as far as I'm concerned.
hint.en.ruleSelf: I cut myself. I did it myself. Without it: I feel tired. We met. Alone: on my own, by myself. Both ways: each other. For a noun: the red one, the big ones.
hint.en.ruleSomeAny: some in a yes sentence and in offers: We've got some eggs. Would you like some tea? any in a no and most questions: There isn't any bread. Have you got any honey? how many with what you count, how much with what you don't: How many sheep? How much honey?
hint.en.ruleStory: What had been going on up to a moment then: had been + -ing: I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn. In a story: The door opened. (next) It was raining. (going on) He had lost his way. (before) He had been walking. (before, for a while)
hint.en.ruleTags: A yes sentence, a no tag: It's cold, isn't it? A no sentence, a yes tag: It isn't far, is it? The sentence's verb or do, does, did: You live here, don't you? To agree: So do I. Neither can I. Short: Yes, I do.
hint.en.ruleThereIs: To say something is there, start with there: There's a tent. There are two tents. Negative There isn't a shop. There aren't any shops. Question Is there a shop? — Yes, there is.
hint.en.ruleThisThat: this, these: here · that, those: there; these, those for more than one. Before a noun or alone: this cup, What's that? In the answer it, they.
hint.en.ruleTime: at a clock time, on a day or a date, in a month, a season, a year or a part of the day: at seven, on Monday, in May, in the morning. half past seven is 7:30, a quarter to eight 7:45; a date: the first of May.
hint.en.ruleTooEnough: too cold: more than you want. warm enough, enough water. too cold to swim. too much salt, too many sheep. a bit, quite, very. as tall as Sam, not as old as the inn.
hint.en.ruleUsedTo: used to + the base form: it was so, and it isn't now. I used to live in Leeds. No: I didn't use to like tea. To ask: Did you use to live here? When, how many times, how long: the past simple, I lived there for five years.
hint.en.ruleWasDoing: was, were + -ing: what was going on. The long one with -ing, the short one in the past simple: I was walking when it started to rain. while with the long one: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
hint.en.ruleWasWere: was for I, he, she, it; were for you, we, they: Jack was on the fell. We were tired. No: wasn't, weren't; to ask: Were you there? — Yes, I was.
hint.en.ruleWho: who: people. which: things. that: both. where: places. whose: his, her, their. The object can go: the cheese Arthur likes. A small word stays at the end: the woman I spoke to.
hint.en.ruleWhoMore: With commas: more about someone known: Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, … No commas: which one: the man who lives by the beck. After a comma who, which, whose. Formal: to whom, in which; after a preposition never that. A whole sentence: …, which was a pity.
hint.en.ruleWillBeDoing: will be + -ing: going on then, This time tomorrow I'll be walking. You think: I think it'll rain. You can see: It's going to rain. Arranged: I'm seeing the doctor on Friday. A timetable: The bus leaves at nine.
hint.en.ruleWillHave: Done by then: will have + the participle: By Friday I'll have finished. After by the time, the present: By the time you get here, we'll have eaten. How long by then: will have been + -ing. by is the last moment, until how long it goes on.
hint.en.ruleWish: Not so now: wish + the past: I have no dog: I wish I had one. Not then: wish + had + the participle: I wish I'd listened. You want it to change: wish + would: I wish it would stop. if only is stronger, the same tenses. It may still happen: I hope it stops.
hint.en.ruleWordBuilding: Not: un-, dis-, in-, im- (p, m), il- (l), ir- (r). A noun: -ness, -ment, -tion, -er. An adjective: -ful, -less, -ous, -able. An adverb: -ly. Alone after a, the a noun; before a noun an adjective; with a verb an adverb.
hint.en.ruleWordOrder: Always subject + verb + object, then place and time: Jack feeds the sheep in the morning. Nothing comes between the verb and its object: We like it very much.
hint.en.ruleWould: What happened again and again: would + the base form: We would walk to school. Normal for me: be used to + -ing: I'm used to getting up early. Becoming normal: get used to: You'll get used to it. It was so, not now: I used to get up early.
hint.en.ruleWouldLike: want to plainly, would like to politely: I want to go. I'd like to go. To offer: Would you like a scone? To ask: Could you …, please? What you like in general: like, love, enjoy, hate + -ing: I enjoy walking.

hint.it.ruleAgree: An adjective takes the gender and number of its noun, even after essere: -o, -a, -i, -e. One in -e has two forms, -e and -i.
hint.it.ruleArticle: Every noun is masculine or feminine, and the article shows it. The: il, lo before s + consonant or z, l' before a vowel; la, l'. A: un, uno; una, un'. Plural: i, gli; le.
hint.it.ruleThereIs: There is: c'è with one thing, ci sono with more. A no puts non in front.
hint.it.ruleQuestions: The question word comes first: chi, che cosa, dove, quando, come, perché, quanto; quanto agrees with its noun. A yes-or-no question is the sentence with a rising voice.
hint.it.ruleWhere: Where and where to: a with a town or home, in with a country, a region or a room, da with a person.
hint.it.ruleBeHave: Essere is to be (sono, sei, è …), avere to have (ho, hai, ha …). Hunger, thirst, fear, cold and your age take avere.
hint.it.ruleImperative: Telling someone to do it: to one person, -are verbs end in -a, the others in -i; to several, the voi form; let's, the noi form. To one, don't is non and the infinitive.
hint.it.ruleNumbers: The tens and the unit make one word; before uno and otto the vowel drops.
hint.it.ruleTime: Hours are plural: sono le tre, alle tre. One o'clock, noon and midnight are singular: è l'una, all'una, a mezzogiorno.
hint.it.ruleLike: Italian says like the other way round: what you like decides the verb. Piace with one thing or a verb, piacciono with more; who likes it is mi, ti, gli, le …
hint.it.ruleFused: Di, a, da, in and su melt with the article after them: del, al, dal, nel, sul; della, alla …; dei, ai … In becomes ne-, di de-. Con and per stay apart.
hint.it.rulePlural: The plural changes the last vowel: -o to -i, -a to -e, -e to -i; the article too: il to i, lo and l' to gli, la to le.
hint.it.rulePresent: The ending says who does it, so the pronoun mostly drops: -o I, -i you, -a or -e he or she, -iamo we, -ate, -ete or -ite you all, -ano or -ono they.
hint.it.ruleTuLei: Who are you talking to? Family, friends and children: tu. An adult you don't know well, the teacher, a shopkeeper: Lei, with the verb of lui and lei.
hint.it.ruleIrregular: The verbs used most are irregular: andare, venire, fare, stare, dare … learn them by heart. Noi always ends in -iamo.
hint.it.ruleCiNe: Ci stands for a place already named (there), ne for some of it or of them, after a number or an amount. Ci vuole with one thing, ci vogliono with more.
hint.it.ruleCompare: Comparing: più or meno before the adjective, di before what it is compared with; the same: come or quanto. Better: migliore with a thing, meglio with a verb.
hint.it.ruleFuture: The future is one word: the infinitive without its last -e, then -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno; in -are verbs the a becomes e. Short ones: sarò, avrò, andrò, farò.
hint.it.ruleImperativePronoun: An order to tu, noi or voi takes the short word on its end; da', di', fa', sta', va' double its first letter. Don't to one: non and the infinitive, the short word on it or before it.
hint.it.ruleImperfect: The imperfetto tells how things were and what used to happen: the infinitive without -re, then -vo, -vi, -va, -vamo, -vate, -vano. Essere: ero, eri, era …
hint.it.ruleTwoPasts: Two pasts in one story: the imperfetto paints what was going on and how things were, the passato prossimo tells what happened, once. After mentre, the imperfetto.
hint.it.ruleModal: After potere, volere and dovere (and sapere, to know how) comes the infinitive, right after them; non goes before the modal.
hint.it.ruleNo: Italian says no twice: non before the verb, the second word after it (mai, niente, nessuno, più, ancora). With nessuno or niente first, as the subject, no non.
hint.it.ruleIrregularParticiple: Many verbs, mostly in -ere, have a participle of their own (fare: fatto; vedere: visto). Learn them in families that sound alike: -tto, -so, -sto, -erto, -nto.
hint.it.rulePartitive: Some: di and the article, as when they melt (del pane, delle mele); un po' di with what you don't count; qualche with the singular.
hint.it.rulePast: The passato prossimo: avere or essere in the present, then the participle. Most verbs take avere; verbs of going and changing, and every reflexive verb, take essere, and then the participle agrees.
hint.it.rulePossessive: A possessive agrees with what is owned, not with the owner, and comes with the article; one family member in the singular drops the article.
hint.it.ruleDirect: Him, her, it, them: lo, la, li, le before the verb, one for each gender and number; lo and la become l' before a vowel.
hint.it.ruleIndirect: To whom: mi, ti, gli (to him), le (to her; Le, polite), ci, vi, right before the verb, and non before them.
hint.it.ruleChe: Che joins two sentences about the same person or thing (who, which, that) and never changes; chi only asks who. After a preposition: cui.
hint.it.ruleReflexive: A reflexive verb is done to yourself: mi, ti, si, ci, vi before the verb, by the person. In the past it takes essere.
hint.it.ruleStare: What is going on right now: stare and the gerund in -ando or -endo, which never changes.
hint.it.ruleSuperlative: The most of all: the article, più and the adjective, the group after di. Very: -issimo on the adjective, agreeing.
hint.it.ruleWould: Asking politely: vorrei (I'd like) with a thing or an infinitive; potrei, potresti, potrebbe (could).
hint.it.ruleConditional: Would: the future's stem and -ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero; in -are verbs the a becomes e. For a wish, advice and what you imagine.
hint.it.ruleSubj: When you want, hope or think something about someone else, che takes the congiuntivo: -are verbs end in -i, the others in -a; short ones have their own. The same person: di and the infinitive.
hint.it.ruleSubjAfter: Some words always bring the congiuntivo after them: è importante che, bisogna che, è meglio che, prima che, senza che, sono contento che. The same person: di and the infinitive.
hint.it.ruleLinking: Each linking word says how two sentences belong together: perché and siccome the reason, quindi what follows, ma and però but, anche se even if, mentre while.
hint.it.ruleReported: Telling what someone says: dice che and the same tense; a question with se, an order with di and the infinitive. After a past (ha detto che), what was so then goes into the imperfetto.
hint.it.ruleFuturePerfect: What will be done first: avere or essere in the future and the participle, after quando, appena or dopo che.
hint.it.ruleGerund: The gerund on its own (-ando, -endo) says while, or by doing it, and never changes; its doer is the main verb's.
hint.it.ruleIndefinite: Someone is qualcuno, something qualcosa. Ogni (every) never changes and takes the singular; tutto agrees and has the article after it.
hint.it.ruleVerbPrep: When a verb brings another along, the second is the infinitive, often with a little word: a after starting, learning, going, helping, trying; di after finishing, stopping, deciding, forgetting.
hint.it.ruleRemote: The passato remoto is the past of fairy tales: -ò, -ì, -é for one, -arono, -irono, -erono for several; fu, ebbe, disse, fece. In the north people say the passato prossimo.
hint.it.rulePassive: The passive: essere and the participle, which agrees like an adjective; who does it comes after da. In the past, essere's own past comes in, and both participles agree.
hint.it.ruleIf: If it can really happen, both halves are in the present or the future. If you only imagine it, se takes the congiuntivo imperfetto and the other half the conditional. Never the conditional after se.
hint.it.ruleDoublePronoun: To whom and what together: the person first, then lo, la, li, le or ne; mi, ti, ci, vi turn their i into e, and gli and le become glie-, written as one word.
hint.it.ruleCui: After a preposition the word is cui, which never changes: in cui, con cui, di cui, a cui. Without a preposition, che.
hint.it.ruleSi: What people do in general: si and the verb of lui and lei; with a plural thing after it, the verb is plural too.
hint.it.ruleAboutTo: About to happen: stare per and the infinitive. Just happened: appena with the passato prossimo, between its two parts.
hint.it.rulePluperfect: What came first in the past: avere or essere in the imperfetto (avevo, ero …) and the participle; with essere it agrees.
hint.it.rulePronominal: Some verbs keep their short words for good: andarsene (me ne vado), farcela (ce la faccio), volerci (ci vuole with one thing, ci vogliono with more).
hint.it.ruleAltered: An ending changes what a word says: small -ino, -etto, -ello; dear -uccio; big -one; bad -accio. -mente makes an adverb, in- the opposite, ri- again.
hint.it.ruleSequence: Which tense after which: a first verb in the present takes the congiuntivo presente, or the passato for what came before; one in the past, or vorrei, the imperfetto, or the trapassato.
hint.it.rulePastConditional: What would have been, and wasn't: avrei or sarei and the participle; with essere it agrees. Told in the past, a future turns into it too.
hint.it.ruleSubjImperfect: After a past, after vorrei che and after se for what you imagine: the congiuntivo imperfetto, -assi, -essi, -issi.
hint.it.ruleSubjAlone: The congiuntivo on its own: a wish with magari, almeno or se solo; a doubt with che.
hint.it.ruleSubjPast: What has already happened, after an opinion, a doubt or a feeling: abbia or sia and the participle; with essere it agrees.
hint.it.ruleSubjPluperfect: What came before a past, after a past or se: avessi or fossi and the participle; with essere it agrees.
hint.it.ruleSubjLinking: These linking words take the congiuntivo: benché, sebbene, nonostante (although), purché (as long as), affinché (so that), a meno che non (unless), come se (as if).
hint.it.ruleConnectives: Words that join a text: tuttavia (however), invece, anzi (on the contrary), in effetti, inoltre; a causa di with a noun. What is known can come first, said again by a short word.
hint.it.ruleReportedPast: After ha detto or disse the tense moves back: the present becomes the imperfetto, the past the trapassato, the future the past conditional; domani becomes il giorno dopo, qui lì.
hint.it.ruleFare: Someone else does it: fare and the infinitive; letting it be: lasciare and the infinitive. The short words go before fare, or on its imperative.
hint.it.ruleGerundPast: What was done first, or why: avendo or essendo and the participle; with essendo it agrees. Both halves have the same doer.
hint.it.ruleInfinitivePast: After doing it, the same doer: dopo aver or dopo essere and the participle; with essere it agrees. The short words join on at the end.
hint.it.ruleParticipleAlone: The participle alone says what was over first: it agrees with the noun after it or, with a verb of essere, with the person.
hint.it.rulePassiveMust: It is being done: venire and the participle, in the simple tenses. It must be done: andare and the participle. The participle agrees with the thing.
hint.it.ruleIfPast: If it had been: se avessi or se fossi and the participle, then avrei or sarei and the participle. Never the conditional after se; still true now: the plain conditional.
hint.it.ruleStory: Telling a story: the imperfetto paints the picture; the passato remoto (in books) or the passato prossimo (in speech) tells what happened.
hint.it.ruleQuale: Il quale, la quale, i quali, le quali are che and cui in a formal voice, agreeing with the noun they stand for; a preposition melts in. Chi is whoever, with the singular.

hint.de.ruleAdjektivDer: After der, die, das: -e in five places (der, die, das in the nominative; die, das in the accusative), -en everywhere else: den großen Hund, dem großen Hund, der kleinen Katze, die großen Hunde. dieser, jeder, welcher the same.
hint.de.ruleAdjektivEin: Where ein, kein, mein have no ending, the adjective takes it: ein großer Hund (der), ein kleines Haus (das, nominative and accusative). Everywhere else as after der: eine kleine Katze, einen großen Hund, einem großen Hund, keine großen Hunde.
hint.de.ruleAdjektivNomen: An adjective as a noun keeps an adjective's endings: der Bekannte, ein Bekannter, dem Bekannten, die Verwandten, zwei Verwandte. After etwas, nichts, viel: -es: etwas Neues. After das, alles: -e: alles Gute.
hint.de.ruleAdjektivNull: No article: the adjective takes der's ending: frischer Käse, frische Milch, frisches Brot, frische Eier; frischen Käse; mit frischem Käse, mit frischer Milch, mit frischen Eiern. After viele, einige and a number too: viele alte Häuser.
hint.de.ruleAdjektivTabelle: The ending shows the case once. The article shows it: -e or -en (der gute, den guten, des guten). It doesn't, or there's none: the adjective does (ein guter, ein gutes, guter, gutem). Genitive with no article: -en, but -er for die and the plural.
hint.de.ruleAdjektivePraep: Learn the chunk: stolz auf, froh über, bekannt für + accusative; zufrieden mit, abhängig von, interessiert an, Angst vor + dative. Worauf? Darauf. Auf wen? Auf ihn. Stolz darauf, dass …
hint.de.ruleAkkusativ: The object is in the accusative. Only der changes: der → den, ein → einen; die and das stay. Pronouns: mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch, sie.
hint.de.ruleAlsOb: als ob, als wenn + the Konjunktiv II, the verb last: Er tut, als ob er schliefe. Just als, the verb next: als wäre er krank. A wish, with doch or nur: Wenn er doch käme! Hätte ich nur Zeit!
hint.de.ruleArtikelGenus: Every noun has a gender: der (masculine), die (feminine), das (neuter); a: ein, eine, ein. In the plural always die. Nouns are written with a capital letter.
hint.de.ruleDativ: After aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu always the dative, and with helfen, danken, geben for who gets it. der, das → dem, die → der, plural die → den, the noun with -n; ein → einem, eine → einer. Pronouns: ich → mir, du → dir, er → ihm, sie → ihr, Sie → Ihnen; the accusative has mich, dich, ihn, sie.
hint.de.ruleDoppelkonnektoren: Added: nicht nur … sondern auch. Both: sowohl … als auch. Neither: weder … noch, with no nicht. One of two: entweder … oder. sondern, oder take no place; noch first place: noch ruft er an.
hint.de.ruleDuSie: du for family, friends and children, Sie (with a capital, plural verb) for adults you don't know well: Wie geht es dir? but Wie geht es Ihnen? Hast du …? but Haben Sie …?
hint.de.ruleFaelle: Four cases show a noun's job: Nominativ (who), Akkusativ (whom), Dativ (to whom), Genitiv (whose). You hear them on the article: der, den, dem, des; die, die, der, der; das, das, dem, des.
hint.de.ruleFormellerBrief: Sehr geehrte Frau Magister Huber, then a small letter. Könnten Sie …? Ich wäre Ihnen dankbar, wenn … Mit freundlichen Grüßen, no comma. Beilage: for what you send along.
hint.de.ruleFragen: The question word comes first, the verb right after it: Wo ist der Hund? Three for where: wo (where), wohin (where to), woher (where from). A yes/no question starts with the verb: Kommst du?
hint.de.ruleGenitiv: Whose: des + -s, der: das Haus des Müllers, die Küche der Wirtin, das Spiel der Kinder. meines Vaters, meiner Mutter. A name: Stefans Hund. After -s, -ß, -z: -es. In talk: von + the dative: das Haus von meinem Vater.
hint.de.ruleImperativ: To one (du): komm! (no du, no -st; e → i stays: nimm!, a → ä doesn't: fahr!). To several (ihr): kommt! Polite: kommen Sie! sein: sei! seid! seien Sie! Separable: steh auf!
hint.de.ruleIndefinitpronomen: People: jemand, niemand, irgendwer; things: etwas, nichts, alles. man takes the er form. Standing alone: einen, keinen; welche for a plural. The same: derselbe, denselben, demselben.
hint.de.ruleIndemSodass: How: indem, dadurch, dass. What came of it: sodass, so … dass. Too much: zu …, um … zu. Without, instead: ohne dass, anstatt dass. The verb goes last in each clause.
hint.de.ruleIndirekteRede: Reporting: Er sagt, er sei krank. The stem + -e: er habe, er komme, er könne. Where it's the present's, the Konjunktiv II: sie hätten, sie kämen. ich becomes er, mein becomes sein. In talk the present is said too.
hint.de.ruleInfinitivZu: After versuchen, anfangen, Lust haben, es ist schön: zu + the verb last. Separable: aufzustehen. What for: um … zu; another person: damit, the verb last. ohne … zu, statt … zu. A modal takes no zu.
hint.de.ruleKeinNicht: kein replaces ein or no article before a noun: Ich habe keinen Hund. Wir haben keine Milch. nicht for everything else: Ich komme nicht. Es ist nicht weit. Das ist nicht der Weg.
hint.de.ruleKonjunktivVergangenheit: The Perfekt with hätte or wäre: Ich hätte geholfen. Ich wäre gekommen. Regret: Hätte ich das nur gewusst! A condition: Wenn ich das gewusst hätte, wäre ich gekommen. A modal verb: Ich hätte kommen können.
hint.de.ruleKonjunktivZwei: The short past with an umlaut and -e: hätte, wäre, könnte, müsste, käme. Every other verb: würde + infinitive. Wishes, Ich hätte gern; asking, Würdest du?; advice, Du solltest; what isn't so, Wenn ich Zeit hätte, käme ich.
hint.de.ruleKonnektoren: und, aber, oder, denn, sondern take no place: …, denn es regnet. deshalb takes first place, the verb follows: …, deshalb bleibt Stefan zu Hause. weil sends the verb last: …, weil es regnet.
hint.de.ruleModalverben: können, müssen, dürfen, sollen, wollen, möchten: the modal verb stands second, the other verb goes last, in the infinitive with no zu: Ich kann gut singen. ich and er have the same form, with no -t: ich will, er will; the plural is regular.
hint.de.ruleModalVermutung: How sure: Das muss Kathi sein. Er dürfte zu Hause sein. Das könnte Stefan sein. Who says so: Er soll reich sein, others; Franz will den Bären gesehen haben, he himself. A guess: Er wird schon angekommen sein.
hint.de.ruleNDeklination: A few masculine nouns take -n or -en in every case but the nominative: -e for a person or an animal (den Kollegen), a few short ones (dem Menschen), -ent, -ist, -at, -graf (dem Studenten). dem Herrn, die Herren. des Namens.
hint.de.ruleNebensatz: After weil, dass, wenn, ob the conjugated verb goes last, with a comma before: …, weil ich müde bin. With two verbs the conjugated one is the last word. Clause first: two verbs meet at the comma: Wenn es schneit, bleiben wir. In talk people also say weil with the verb second; writing wants it last.
hint.de.ruleNomenVerb: Each noun has its verb: eine Frage stellen, eine Rolle spielen, Hilfe leisten, Bescheid sagen. zur Verfügung stellen is giving, zur Verfügung stehen being there. No: keine Entscheidung, nicht in Frage.
hint.de.ruleNominalisierung: das Kochen, beim Kochen. -ung, -heit, -keit: always die. A clause becomes a phrase: weil → wegen des Regens; obwohl → trotz des Regens; als ich ankam → bei meiner Ankunft; bevor → vor dem Essen; nachdem → nach dem Essen.
hint.de.ruleObwohlTrotzdem: obwohl sends the verb last: …, obwohl es regnet. First in the sentence: Obwohl es regnet, gehen wir. trotzdem takes first place, the verb next: Es regnet, trotzdem gehen wir. Like weil and deshalb, with the opposite meaning.
hint.de.ruleOesterreichisch: heuer, Jänner, Paradeiser, Erdäpfel, Topfen, Sessel, Kasten; ich bin gesessen; um fünf Euro; das geht sich aus. Germany's forms are right too. Spoken: lei, nit, eppes.
hint.de.ruleOrdinalzahlen: To 19 -te, from 20 -ste; erste, dritte, siebte, achte are special. der erste Mai, but am ersten Mai, vom ersten bis zum dritten. vor zwei Tagen (ago), in einer Woche. Austria: Jänner, heuer.
hint.de.rulePartizipAdjektiv: Before a noun, with an adjective's ending. Partizip I (infinitive + d), going on now: der spielende Hund. Partizip II, done: das gebackene Brot; with a sein verb of change, happened: der gefallene Schnee.
hint.de.rulePartizipZwei: ge-…-t (gekauft), ge-…-en (getrunken), mixed (gebracht). Separable: ge in the middle (aufgestanden). be-, ver-, er-, ent-, -ieren: no ge- (verstanden, telefoniert). sein for moving and change, Austria also ist gesessen.
hint.de.rulePartizipialattribut: The article waits for its noun; right before it, the participle; between them, what belongs to it. Partizip I: mostly the present (der Mann, der am Bach steht). Partizip II: wurde or hat (der Traktor, der repariert wurde); with a sein verb, ist.
hint.de.rulePassiv: werden + the participle, last: Das Brot wird gebacken. Die Äpfel werden gepflückt. Past: wurde, wurden. Who: von + dative. Den becomes der: Der Most wird gepresst. Everyday: Man presst den Most.
hint.de.rulePassivErsatz: It can be done: Das lässt sich machen. Das ist zu machen. Das ist machbar. Das kann man machen. It must be done: Die Rechnung ist zu bezahlen. The action: wird geöffnet; the state: ist geöffnet.
hint.de.rulePassivZeiten: ist + the participle + worden: Das Haus ist gebaut worden. Before: war gebaut worden. A modal, then the participle + werden: Das muss gemacht werden. Die Straße müsste repariert werden.
hint.de.rulePerfekt: A helper in second place and the participle last: Ich habe gelernt. Wir sind gefahren. Most verbs take haben; moving from place to place and change take sein, as do sein and bleiben. In Austria sitzen, stehen and liegen take sein too: ich bin gesessen. In talk this is the usual past.
hint.de.rulePlural: In the plural der, die and das all become die. Learn the ending with the noun: -e (die Arme), umlaut + -e (die Bänke), -er (die Kinder), -n, -en (die Taschen, die Frauen), -s (die Autos).
hint.de.rulePlusquamperfekt: What came first: hatte or war + the participle: Als Stefan kam, hatte Kathi schon gekocht. haben → hatte, sein → war. nachdem steps back: Nachdem ich gegessen hatte, ging ich. With a present: Nachdem ich gegessen habe, gehe ich.
hint.de.rulePossessiv: The owner picks the word: mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, ihr, Ihr. The noun picks the ending, as ein: mein Hund, meine Katze, meine Schafe; a der noun in the accusative meinen. Kathi → ihr, Toni → sein.
hint.de.rulePraepAkk: Always the accusative: bis, durch, für, gegen, ohne, um. Only a der noun shows it: für den Opa, ohne einen Hut, but für die Oma, durch das Dorf. Pronouns: für mich, ohne dich, gegen ihn. Often no article: ohne Zucker, bis Montag.
hint.de.rulePraepDat: Always the dative: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu. zum (zu dem), zur (zu der), beim, vom. Wo? bei Kathi. Wohin? zu Kathi. Woher? von Kathi. A town: nach Villach. Home: nach Hause, zu Hause.
hint.de.rulePraepGen: Take the genitive (der, das → des, die → der): wegen, trotz, während, statt, innerhalb, außerhalb: wegen des Sturms, trotz der Kälte. A noun alone stays bare: statt Wein. In talk, the dative is right too: wegen dem Sturm. A pronoun: wegen mir.
hint.de.rulePraesens: Take the stem and add: ich -e, du -st, er/sie/es -t, wir -en, ihr -t, sie/Sie -en: spiele, spielst, spielt, spielen, spielt, spielen. The pronoun is always said.
hint.de.rulePraeteritum: For tales and writing. Regular -te: sagte, arbeitete. Strong, a new vowel: ging, kam, sah. Mixed, both: dachte, brachte. ich = er; du -st, wir and sie -en, ihr -t. In talk, Austria says the Perfekt: ist gegangen.
hint.de.rulePraeteritumKurz: war, warst, war, waren, wart, waren. hatte, hattest, hatte, hatten, hattet, hatten. Modals: -te and no umlaut: konnte, musste, durfte, wollte, sollte, mochte. es gibt → es gab, always singular. The other verb at the end.
hint.de.rulePronomenDativ: Dative: mir, dir, ihm, ihr, ihm, uns, euch, ihnen, Ihnen. helfen, danken, gefallen, schmecken, gehören take only it: Ich helfe dir. Das gefällt mir. Es geht mir gut. Sehen, kennen, suchen take mich, dich, ihn.
hint.de.ruleReflexiveVerben: mich, dich, sich, uns, euch, sich, right after the verb. Another object: mir, dir (Ich wasche mir die Hände), the others stay. The Perfekt with haben: Ich habe mich gefreut.
hint.de.ruleRelativsatz: The gender from the noun, the case from its own clause, the verb last: der Mann, der kommt; den ich kenne; dem ich helfe. Dative plural: denen. A preposition first: mit dem, für den. A place: wo. After alles, nichts, etwas: was.
hint.de.ruleSatzbau: Pronouns first: es ihm, ihm den Apfel, ihn dem Kind. Two nouns: dem Kind den Apfel. Then time, cause, manner, place. nicht last, or before a second verb, a place, an adjective.
hint.de.ruleSeinHaben: sein (to be): ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie/Sie sind. haben (to have): ich habe, du hast, er/sie/es hat, wir haben, ihr habt, sie/Sie haben.
hint.de.ruleStehenStellen: Where it is, the dative: stehen, liegen, sitzen: Das Glas steht auf dem Tisch. Putting it there, an object and the accusative: stellen, legen, setzen: Ich stelle das Glas auf den Tisch. hängen is both: the case tells.
hint.de.ruleSteigerung: More: -er als (schneller als), often with an umlaut (älter, größer). The same: so … wie. The most: am -sten (am schnellsten), with an e after -t, -ß, -z (am ältesten). gut, besser, am besten; gern, lieber, am liebsten; viel, mehr, am meisten.
hint.de.ruleTemporalsaetze: Verb last. als: one time in the past. wenn: every time, now, later. während: at the same time. bevor: before. bis: until. seit: since, the present while it still goes on. Clause first: the main verb at the comma: Als ich klein war, wohnte ich …
hint.de.ruleTrennbareVerben: Many verbs have a little word that comes off: aufstehen, anrufen, mitbringen. The verb stands second and the little word goes last: Ich rufe dich an. At the end they join again: after a modal verb, after weil and dass, and in the participle with ge in the middle: angerufen. be-, ver-, er- never come off.
hint.de.ruleUhrzeit: halb acht = 7:30 (towards eight); Viertel nach sieben 7:15, Viertel vor acht 7:45 (Austria also viertel acht, dreiviertel acht). um + a time, am + a day, im + a month: um sieben, am Montag, im Jänner.
hint.de.ruleVerbenPraep: One chunk with its case. Accusative: warten auf, denken an, sich freuen auf (ahead), sich freuen über (here), sprechen über. Dative: sprechen mit, Angst haben vor, erzählen von, träumen von.
hint.de.ruleVokalwechsel: Only du and er/sie/es change: a → ä (fährst), au → äu (läuft), e → i (sprichst, isst, nimmt), e → ie (siehst, liest). ich, wir, ihr and sie keep the vowel: ihr fahrt.
hint.de.ruleWechsel: in, an, auf, über, unter, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen take two cases. Where something is (Wo?): the dative: sein, stehen, liegen, sitzen. Where it goes (Wohin?): the accusative: gehen, fahren, stellen, legen.
hint.de.ruleWerdenFutur: werde, wirst, wird, werden, werdet, werden. + an adjective or a noun: to become, Es wird kalt. + an infinitive at the end: the future, Ich werde dir helfen. With wohl: a guess, Er wird wohl schlafen. Mostly the present is enough: Morgen fahre ich.
hint.de.ruleWoDaWoerter: A thing: wo-, da- + the preposition: worauf? darauf; wofür? dafür; womit? damit. An r before a vowel: woran, darüber. A person: the preposition + a pronoun: auf wen? auf ihn; mit wem? mit ihr.
hint.de.ruleWortstellung: In a statement the verb stands second: Oma Resi backt heute. Anything can come first, and the subject then moves behind the verb: Heute backt Oma Resi.
hint.de.ruleZahlen: 13–19 add -zehn (sechzehn, siebzehn lose letters), the tens -zig (dreißig with ß); from 21 the one first, one word: einundzwanzig. Counting eins, before a noun ein, eine. Wie viel? an amount, Wie viele? + plural.
hint.de.ruleZwarAber: No place: aber, doch. First place, the verb next: zwar, allerdings, dennoch, einerseits, andererseits. The verb last: auch wenn, selbst wenn, während, wohingegen, obwohl.
hintSay.afterNumber: After «{word}», {cat, select, one {one} two {two} few {three or four} other {five and up}}:
hintSay.case: the missing word goes into the {case}.
hintSay.number: {cat, select, one {the noun stays in the singular.} two {the noun takes the dual.} few {the noun takes the plural.} other {the noun goes into the genitive plural.}}
hintSay.ruleAdverb: How something is done takes the adverb, most often ending in o, not the adjective.
hintSay.ruleAgree: The adjective takes its noun's gender and number: masculine, feminine or neuter.
hintSay.ruleAspect: Going on, or again and again, takes the imperfective; done once, to the end, the perfective.
hintSay.ruleStems: Some nouns grow their stem in the other cases.
hintSay.ruleDualCases: Two in a case take the dual's own endings.
hintSay.ruleAspectTenses: Done once, to the end: the perfective; going on, again and again, or don't: the imperfective, in every tense.
hintSay.ruleDefinite: One already known takes the definite form in -i; a new one, the plain form.
hintSay.ruleClauses: A clause joins the sentence with a word that says how: the cause, a condition, an aim, what came of it.
hintSay.ruleBiti: «Biti», to be, takes the person: one form for one, another for several.
hintSay.ruleCases: Each of the six cases answers its own question: ask the one the missing word answers.
hintSay.ruleClitics: The short words go second in the sentence, in a fixed order.
hintSay.ruleComparative: Comparing takes the comparative; the most puts «naj» in front.
hintSay.ruleDual: Exactly two people or things take the dual, with its own endings.
hintSay.ruleFuture: The future is the future of «biti» with the l-form.
hintSay.ruleGender: Every noun has a gender, mostly told by its ending, and pronouns and adjectives follow it.
hintSay.ruleImperative: Telling someone to do it takes the imperative, its ending by whom you tell.
hintSay.ruleJoining: Each joining word joins two sentences its own way.
hintSay.ruleKi: «Ki» is the same for all; a short pronoun after it says the case.
hintSay.ruleModal: After must, may, want to or know how to comes the infinitive.
hintSay.ruleNoTwice: Slovene says no twice: «ne» with «nič», «nihče» or «nikoli».
hintSay.ruleNumberAgrees: The number agrees with its noun's gender: «en, ena, eno»; «dva, dve»; «trije, tri».
hintSay.ruleNumbers: After a number: one, the singular; two, the dual; three and four, the plural; five and up, the genitive plural.
hintSay.ruleOrdinal: Which one in a row takes the ordinal, which agrees like an adjective.
hintSay.rulePast: The past is «biti» in the present with the l-form, which takes the doer's gender.
hintSay.rulePerson: The verb's ending says who does it.
hintSay.rulePlural: Three or more take the plural, two take the dual.
hintSay.rulePronouns: A personal pronoun has a long form, for emphasis and after a preposition, and a short one otherwise.
hintSay.ruleQuestions: Each question word asks something else: «kje?» where, «kam?» where to, «od kod?» where from.
hintSay.ruleReflexive: Some verbs come with «se», which goes second in the sentence.
hintSay.ruleReported: Reported speech takes «da» for a statement, «naj» for a wish, «ali» for a question.
hintSay.ruleSupine: After a verb of going comes the supine: the infinitive without its last i.
hintSay.ruleSvoj: What belongs to the one who does it takes «svoj», whoever it is.
hintSay.ruleTiVi: Someone older, a stranger, in a shop: «vi»; a friend, a child, family: «ti».
hintSay.ruleWhen: An hour takes «ob» and the locative, a day «v» and the accusative.
hintSay.ruleWhere: Where something is: «v, na, ob, pri» take the locative; «pod, nad, pred, za, med» the instrumental.
hintSay.ruleWhereTo: Where something goes: «v, na, pod, za» take the accusative; «k» the dative.
hintSay.ruleTimeNoPrep: A date takes the genitive; this, every and how long take the accusative.
hintSay.ruleFeelings: Who feels it takes the dative or the accusative, by the word of feeling.
hintSay.rulePluralCases: The plural has its own ending in each case.
hintSay.ruleWhose: A possessive agrees with what is owned, like an adjective.
hintSay.ruleNumberVerb: From five on the verb is singular and neuter; with two, the dual; with three or four, the plural.
hintSay.ruleIfWould: Imagined or past: «bi» with the l-form in both halves; a real chance: the future.
hintSay.ruleCliticOrder: The short words go second in the sentence, always in the same order.
hintSay.ruleVerbalNoun: A verbal noun ends in -anje, -enje or -tje, is neuter, and takes the genitive after it.
hintSay.ruleIndefinite: Some, no and every each have their own beginning; a no-word keeps the no before the verb.
hintSay.rulePassive: «Biti» with the form in -n or -t says how something is after it was done.
hintSay.ruleCompareFull: Each way of comparing has its own words: as … as, much more, as … as possible, the more … the more.
hintSay.rulePluperfect: What had happened before takes «biti» in the past with the l-form.
hintSay.ruleClausesMore: Each joining word says how its clause belongs: although, while, until, without, as if.
hintSay.ruleIdioms: An idiom means more than its words: its words stay, only the verb and the person change.
hintSay.ruleNumberWords: How many times, what kind, how many: each has its own number word.
hintSay.ruleGerund: The form in -e, -aje, -eč or -oč says how, and never changes.
hintSay.ruleDiminutive: A little one ends in -ica, -ek or -ce, keeps its gender and declines by its new ending.
hintSay.ruleCommands: Let's ends in -va or -mo, let him takes «naj», and don't takes the imperfective.
hintSay.ruleParticiple: A participle agrees with its noun like an adjective.
hintSay.ruleWordFamily: One root, many words: the ending says who, where or what it is like.
hintSay.rulePrefix: A prefix makes the verb perfective; for what goes on, the new imperfective.
hintSay.ruleTwoCases: The accusative says where to or what you go for; the locative or the instrumental, where.
hintSay.ruleSpoken: Spoken and written forms are both right, each in its place.
hintSay.ruleFormalLetter: A formal letter says «Vi» with a capital, the verb in the plural.
hintSay.rulePastConditional: What would have been takes «bil bi» with the l-form.
hintSay.ruleImpersonal: Without a subject the verb is in the third person singular, neuter in the past.
hintSay.ruleWhichWhose: «Kateri» takes the case of its own clause.
hintSay.ruleWordOrder: What is known comes first, the news last, the short words second.
hintSay.en.ruleAdverbs: A thing takes the adjective, how it is done the adverb: «slow», «slowly».
hintSay.en.ruleArticles: «an» before a vowel sound, «a» before any other: «an apple», «a horse».
hintSay.en.ruleAskedWhere: After «asked where», the order of a statement: «where I lived».
hintSay.en.ruleBe: «I am», «he is», «they are»: the verb goes with who.
hintSay.en.ruleCan: After «can» the verb stays as it is, the same for everyone.
hintSay.en.ruleCollocations: Some words go together: «make a mistake», «do your best».
hintSay.en.ruleCompare: Short words take «-er» and «the -est», long ones «more» and «the most».
hintSay.en.ruleContrast: «although» with a sentence, «despite» with a noun or «-ing».
hintSay.en.ruleDo: A question and a no take «do» or «does», and the verb stays as it is.
hintSay.en.ruleEmphasis: To stress it: «It was … who», «What I need is», «did» with the base form.
hintSay.en.ruleForSince: «for» says how long, «since» when it began.
hintSay.en.ruleFormal: A formal letter ends «Yours faithfully» or «Yours sincerely»; to a friend, «Cheers».
hintSay.en.ruleFuture: A plan: «going to»; decided now or promised: «will».
hintSay.en.ruleGuess: Perhaps: «might»; sure it is: «must»; sure it isn't: «can't».
hintSay.en.ruleHaveItDone: Someone does it for you: «have», the thing, and the participle.
hintSay.en.ruleIfHad: What didn't happen: «if» with «had», then «would have».
hintSay.en.ruleIfWould: What isn't so: «if» with the past, then «would».
hintSay.en.ruleImperatives: An order is the base form, without «you»; the no is «don't».
hintSay.en.ruleIndefinite: «some-» in a yes sentence, «any-» in a no or a question, «no-» with a yes verb.
hintSay.en.ruleMixedIf: Then and now mixed: «If I'd listened, I'd be there now.»
hintSay.en.ruleMust: «have to» and «must»: you need to; «mustn't»: not allowed; «don't have to»: no need.
hintSay.en.ruleNow: What's going on now: «am», «is» or «are» with the «-ing» form.
hintSay.en.ruleNumbers: Thirteen to nineteen end in «-teen», the tens in «-ty».
hintSay.en.ruleObjectPronouns: After a verb or a preposition: «me», «him», «her», «us», «them».
hintSay.en.ruleParticipleClauses: A clause with «-ing» or the participle, with one subject for both halves.
hintSay.en.rulePassive: The passive: a form of «be» with the participle; who did it comes after «by».
hintSay.en.rulePassiveMore: The passive in every tense: «has been», «is being», «will be» with the participle.
hintSay.en.rulePast: Finished: «-ed», or a past of its own; questions and the no take «did».
hintSay.en.rulePastModals: Looking back: a modal with «have» and the participle.
hintSay.en.rulePastPerfect: What came earlier still: «had» with the participle.
hintSay.en.rulePatterns: Each verb has its pattern: «decide to», «enjoy» with «-ing».
hintSay.en.rulePerfect: «have» or «has» with the past participle, from the past up to now.
hintSay.en.rulePerfectGoingOn: Going on up to now: «have been» with «-ing».
hintSay.en.rulePhrasal: A verb and a small word make a new meaning; a pronoun goes between: «turn it off».
hintSay.en.rulePhrasalMore: Three words stay together; «look forward to» takes «-ing».
hintSay.en.rulePlace: «in» inside, «on» on top, «at» a place as a point.
hintSay.en.rulePlurals: Most nouns add «-s»; some have a plural of their own, like «children» and «sheep».
hintSay.en.rulePossessive: The owner takes an apostrophe and s, «Jack's dog»; before a noun «my», alone «mine».
hintSay.en.rulePronouns: English always says who does it: «I», «you», «he», «she», «it», «we», «they».
hintSay.en.ruleReported: Told later, the tense moves one step back: «is» becomes «was».
hintSay.en.ruleReporting: Each reporting verb has its pattern: «promised to», «suggested» with «-ing».
hintSay.en.ruleResult: «so» with an adjective, «such a» with a noun, then «that».
hintSay.en.ruleSomeAny: «some» in a yes sentence, «any» in a no or a question.
hintSay.en.ruleStory: In a story: what happened, the past simple; what came before, «had» with the participle.
hintSay.en.ruleTags: A yes sentence takes a no tag, a no sentence a yes tag: «isn't it?», «is it?».
hintSay.en.ruleThereIs: «There's» with one thing, «there are» with more.
hintSay.en.ruleThisThat: «this» and «these» are here, «that» and «those» there; «these» and «those» for more than one.
hintSay.en.ruleTime: «at» a clock time, «on» a day, «in» a month or a year.
hintSay.en.ruleTooEnough: «too» is more than you want; «enough» comes after an adjective.
hintSay.en.ruleUsedTo: It was so and isn't now: «used to» with the base form.
hintSay.en.ruleWasDoing: What was going on: «was» or «were» with the «-ing» form.
hintSay.en.ruleWho: «who» for people, «which» for things, «where» for places.
hintSay.en.ruleWhoMore: With commas, more about someone known; after a comma, never «that».
hintSay.en.ruleWillBeDoing: Going on at a time then: «will be» with «-ing».
hintSay.en.ruleWillHave: Done by then: «will have» with the participle.
hintSay.en.ruleWish: Not so now: «wish» with the past; not so then: «wish» with «had».
hintSay.en.ruleWordBuilding: Endings make a noun, an adjective or an adverb: «-ness», «-ful», «-ly».
hintSay.en.ruleWordOrder: Who, the verb, then what: «Jack feeds the sheep».
hintSay.en.ruleWould: Again and again in the past: «would»; normal for me: «be used to» with «-ing».
hintSay.en.ruleWouldLike: Politely: «would like to»; what you like doing: «enjoy» with «-ing».
hintSay.it.ruleAgree: The adjective takes its noun's gender and number: «-o», «-a», «-i», «-e».
hintSay.it.ruleArticle: Every noun is masculine or feminine; the article goes by its gender, its number and its first sound.
hintSay.it.ruleThereIs: «C'è» with one thing, «ci sono» with more.
hintSay.it.ruleQuestions: The question word comes first, and «quanto» agrees with its noun.
hintSay.it.ruleWhere: «a» with a town, «in» with a country or a room, «da» with a person.
hintSay.it.ruleBeHave: «Essere» is to be, «avere» to have; hunger, thirst, cold and your age take «avere».
hintSay.it.ruleImperative: To one person the verb ends in «-a» or «-i», to several it takes the «voi» form; don't is «non» with the infinitive.
hintSay.it.ruleNumbers: The tens and the unit make one word; before «uno» and «otto» the vowel drops.
hintSay.it.ruleTime: Hours are plural, «alle tre»; one o'clock, noon and midnight are singular, «all'una».
hintSay.it.ruleLike: What you like decides the verb: «piace» with one thing, «piacciono» with more.
hintSay.it.ruleFused: «di», «a», «da», «in» and «su» melt with the article after them.
hintSay.it.rulePlural: In the plural «-o» becomes «-i», «-a» becomes «-e», «-e» becomes «-i».
hintSay.it.rulePresent: The verb's ending says who does it: «-o» I, «-i» you, «-iamo» we.
hintSay.it.ruleTuLei: Family, friends and children: «tu»; an adult you don't know well: «Lei».
hintSay.it.ruleIrregular: The most used verbs are irregular; «noi» always ends in «-iamo».
hintSay.it.ruleCiNe: «Ci» is there, «ne» is some of it; «ci vuole» with one thing, «ci vogliono» with more.
hintSay.it.ruleCompare: More is «più», less «meno», than is «di»; the same is «come».
hintSay.it.ruleImperativePronoun: In an order the short word goes on the end of the verb; don't is «non» with the infinitive.
hintSay.it.ruleImperfect: How things were, and what happened again and again: «-vo», «-vi», «-va».
hintSay.it.ruleTwoPasts: What was going on takes the «imperfetto»; what happened, once, the «passato prossimo».
hintSay.it.ruleNo: Italian says no twice: «non» with «mai», «niente» or «nessuno».
hintSay.it.ruleIrregularParticiple: Many verbs have a participle of their own, like «fatto», «preso», «visto».
hintSay.it.rulePartitive: Some is «di» with the article; «qualche» takes the singular.
hintSay.it.rulePast: «avere» or «essere» with the participle; going and changing take «essere», and then the participle agrees.
hintSay.it.rulePossessive: The possessive agrees with what is owned, and takes the article, except with one family member.
hintSay.it.ruleDirect: «lo», «la», «li», «le» stand for what was named, by its gender and number.
hintSay.it.ruleIndirect: To whom: «mi», «ti», «gli», «le», right before the verb.
hintSay.it.ruleChe: «Che» is who, which and that, and never changes; «chi» only asks.
hintSay.it.ruleReflexive: The short word goes with the person, «mi lavo», «ti lavi»; in the past the verb takes «essere».
hintSay.it.ruleStare: What goes on right now: «stare» with the form in «-ando» or «-endo».
hintSay.it.ruleSuperlative: The most is the article, «più» and the adjective; very is «-issimo».
hintSay.it.ruleWould: Ask politely with «vorrei» and a thing or the infinitive.
hintSay.it.ruleConditional: Would takes «-ei», «-esti», «-ebbe» on the future's stem.
hintSay.it.ruleSubj: Wanting, hoping or thinking something of someone else: «che» with the «congiuntivo».
hintSay.it.ruleSubjAfter: After «è importante che», «bisogna che» or «prima che» comes the «congiuntivo».
hintSay.it.ruleLinking: Each linking word says how the two halves belong together.
hintSay.it.ruleReported: «dice che» keeps the tense; after «ha detto che», what was so goes into the «imperfetto».
hintSay.it.ruleFuturePerfect: What will be done first takes the future of «avere» or «essere» with the participle.
hintSay.it.ruleGerund: The form in «-ando» or «-endo» says while or how, and never changes.
hintSay.it.ruleIndefinite: «Ogni» takes the singular; «tutto» agrees and has the article after it.
hintSay.it.ruleVerbPrep: Each verb brings its own little word: «a» after starting, «di» after finishing.
hintSay.it.rulePassive: The passive is «essere» with the participle, which agrees with the thing.
hintSay.it.ruleIf: Real: the present after «se»; imagined: the «congiuntivo» after «se» and the conditional in the other half.
hintSay.it.ruleCui: After a preposition comes «cui»; without one, «che».
hintSay.it.ruleSi: «Si» takes the verb of one person; a plural thing makes the verb plural.
hintSay.it.ruleAboutTo: About to: «stare per» with the infinitive; just now: «appena».
hintSay.it.rulePluperfect: What came first in the past: «avevo» or «ero» with the participle.
hintSay.it.rulePronominal: Some verbs keep their short words: «me ne vado», «ce la faccio».
hintSay.it.ruleAltered: Small is «-ino» or «-etto», big «-one», bad «-accio»; «-mente» says how.
hintSay.it.ruleSequence: First verb now: the «congiuntivo presente»; first verb in the past: the «imperfetto».
hintSay.it.rulePastConditional: What would have been: «avrei» or «sarei» with the participle.
hintSay.it.ruleSubjImperfect: After a past, «vorrei che» or «se»: the forms in «-assi», «-essi», «-issi».
hintSay.it.ruleSubjAlone: A wish with «magari», or a doubt with «che»: the «congiuntivo» on its own.
hintSay.it.ruleSubjPast: What has already happened: «abbia» or «sia» with the participle.
hintSay.it.ruleSubjPluperfect: What came before a past: «avessi» or «fossi» with the participle.
hintSay.it.ruleConnectives: Each joining word says how the next sentence belongs to the one before.
hintSay.it.ruleReportedPast: After «ha detto» or «disse» the tense moves back.
hintSay.it.ruleFare: «fare» or «lasciare» with the infinitive: someone else does it, or is let.
hintSay.it.ruleGerundPast: What was done first: «avendo» or «essendo» with the participle.
hintSay.it.ruleInfinitivePast: After doing it: «dopo aver» or «dopo essere» with the participle.
hintSay.it.ruleParticipleAlone: The participle alone says what was over first, and agrees with its noun.
hintSay.it.rulePassiveMust: «viene» with the participle: it is done; «va»: it must be done.
hintSay.it.ruleIfPast: If it had been: «se avessi» with the participle, then «avrei» or «sarei».
hintSay.it.ruleStory: The «imperfetto» paints the picture; the «remoto» or the «prossimo» tells what happened.
hintSay.it.ruleQuale: «Il quale» agrees with the noun it stands for; «chi» is whoever.
hintSay.it.habit: When: «{word}», again and again or going on.
hintSay.de.ruleAdjektivDer: After the article: «-e» in five places, «-en» everywhere else.
hintSay.de.ruleAdjektivEin: Where «ein» has no ending, the adjective takes it.
hintSay.de.ruleAdjektivNomen: An adjective used as a noun keeps an adjective's endings.
hintSay.de.ruleAdjektivNull: With no article the adjective takes the article's ending.
hintSay.de.ruleAdjektivTabelle: The ending shows the case once: on the article, or else on the adjective.
hintSay.de.ruleAdjektivePraep: Learn the adjective with its preposition and its case.
hintSay.de.ruleAkkusativ: What the verb acts on goes into the accusative; only masculine words change.
hintSay.de.ruleAlsOb: «als ob» with the Konjunktiv, the verb last; just «als», the verb next.
hintSay.de.ruleArtikelGenus: Every noun has its gender: learn its article with it.
hintSay.de.ruleDativ: Who gets something or is helped goes into the dative; so does what follows some prepositions.
hintSay.de.ruleDoppelkonnektoren: These words come in pairs: learn both halves together.
hintSay.de.ruleDuSie: Family, friends and children: «du»; adults you don't know well: «Sie».
hintSay.de.ruleFaelle: The case shows a noun's job, and you hear it on the article.
hintSay.de.ruleFormellerBrief: A formal letter has its fixed greeting and ending.
hintSay.de.ruleFragen: The question word comes first, the verb right after it.
hintSay.de.ruleGenitiv: Whose: the genitive; in talk «von» with the dative is right too.
hintSay.de.ruleImperativ: To one person the verb's stem, to several the «ihr» form, politely with «Sie».
hintSay.de.ruleIndefinitpronomen: «man» takes the «er» form; standing alone, these words keep their endings.
hintSay.de.ruleIndemSodass: How something happens, or what came of it: the verb goes last.
hintSay.de.ruleIndirekteRede: Reporting someone: the Konjunktiv; in talk the present is said too.
hintSay.de.ruleInfinitivZu: «zu» goes before the last verb; a modal takes no «zu».
hintSay.de.ruleKeinNicht: Before a noun with no article or with «ein»: «kein»; everything else: «nicht».
hintSay.de.ruleKonjunktivVergangenheit: Imagined about the past: the Konjunktiv of the helper with the participle.
hintSay.de.ruleKonjunktivZwei: For what isn't so, or to ask politely: the Konjunktiv.
hintSay.de.ruleKonnektoren: «und» and «aber» take no place, «deshalb» takes first place, «weil» sends the verb last.
hintSay.de.ruleModalverben: The modal verb stands second, the other verb last, as it is in the dictionary.
hintSay.de.ruleModalVermutung: The modal verb says how sure you are, or who says so.
hintSay.de.ruleNDeklination: A few masculine nouns take an «-n» in every case but the nominative.
hintSay.de.ruleNebensatz: After «dass» or «wenn» the verb goes last.
hintSay.de.ruleNomenVerb: Each noun has its verb: learn them together.
hintSay.de.ruleNominalisierung: A verb as a noun is a «das» word, with a capital.
hintSay.de.ruleObwohlTrotzdem: «obwohl» sends the verb last, «trotzdem» has the verb next.
hintSay.de.ruleOesterreichisch: Austrian forms are right, and Germany's are too.
hintSay.de.rulePartizipAdjektiv: Going on now: the infinitive with «-d»; done: the participle.
hintSay.de.rulePartizipZwei: «ge-» in front, «-t» or «-en» at the end; with «be-», «ver-» or «-ieren» no «ge-».
hintSay.de.rulePartizipialattribut: The article waits for its noun; the participle stands right before it.
hintSay.de.rulePassiv: «werden» and the participle: it is done to it.
hintSay.de.rulePassivErsatz: It can be done: «lässt sich», «ist zu», or «kann man».
hintSay.de.rulePassivZeiten: The participle with «worden»; after a modal, with «werden».
hintSay.de.rulePerfekt: A helper in second place, the participle last; moving and changing take «sein».
hintSay.de.rulePlural: In the plural the article is always «die»; learn each noun's ending with it.
hintSay.de.rulePlusquamperfekt: What came first: the short past of the helper with the participle.
hintSay.de.rulePossessiv: The owner picks the word, the noun picks its ending.
hintSay.de.rulePraepAkk: After these prepositions always the accusative.
hintSay.de.rulePraepDat: After these prepositions always the dative.
hintSay.de.rulePraepGen: In writing the genitive; in talk the dative is right too.
hintSay.de.rulePraesens: The ending goes with who does it.
hintSay.de.rulePraeteritum: For tales and writing; in talk Austria says the Perfekt.
hintSay.de.rulePraeteritumKurz: «war», «hatte» and the modal verbs are said in the short past.
hintSay.de.ruleReflexiveVerben: With another object in the sentence it becomes the dative.
hintSay.de.ruleRelativsatz: The gender from the noun, the case from its own clause, the verb last.
hintSay.de.ruleSatzbau: Pronouns first, then time, cause, manner, place.
hintSay.de.ruleSeinHaben: «sein» and «haben» change with who: learn them by heart.
hintSay.de.ruleStehenStellen: Where it is: «stehen», «liegen»; putting it there: «stellen», «legen».
hintSay.de.ruleTemporalsaetze: One time in the past, or every time, now or later: the verb goes last.
hintSay.de.ruleTrennbareVerben: In a statement the little word goes last; in the participle «ge» goes in the middle.
hintSay.de.ruleUhrzeit: «um» with a time, «am» with a day, «im» with a month.
hintSay.de.ruleVerbenPraep: Learn the verb with its preposition and its case.
hintSay.de.ruleVokalwechsel: Only «du» and «er, sie, es» change the vowel.
hintSay.de.ruleWerdenFutur: «werden» with an infinitive at the end: the future.
hintSay.de.ruleWoDaWoerter: A thing: «da-» or «wo-» with the preposition; a person: the preposition and a pronoun.
hintSay.de.ruleWortstellung: In a statement the verb stands second.
hintSay.de.ruleZahlen: From twenty-one the one comes first, all in one word.
hintSay.de.ruleZwarAber: «zwar» takes first place, the verb next; «aber» takes no place.

numbers.why.compound: **{n}** → **{ones}** + **in** + **{tens}** = **{word}**: the ones first ({o} + {t}), joined by in, in one word.
numbers.why.big: **{n}** → **{word}**: the hundreds and the thousands apart, up to 99 one word.
numbers.why.order: Slovene says the ones first: **{word}** is {o} + {t} (**{ones}**-**in**-**{tens}**), not *{wrong}*.
numbers.why.spacing: Up to 99 one word, the hundreds and the thousands apart: **{word}**.
numbers.why.date: **{day}.** {month} → **{ordinal}** {month}: a date's day is the ordinal (1. prvi, 2. drugi, 3. tretji, 4. četrti, 7. sedmi, 8. osmi; else the number + -i).
numbers.why.hour: **{time}** → **{said}**: ob and the hour in -ih (ob dveh, ob treh).
numbers.why.half: **{time}** → **{said}**: half counts towards the next hour (pol + {next}).
numbers.it.tip: The tens first, then the ones, all in one word: ventisette (20 + 7).
numbers.it.why.teen: **{n}** → **{word}**: 11 to 16 end in -dici, from 17 they begin with dici-.
numbers.it.why.tens: **{n}** → **{word}**: from 40 on the tens end in -anta (quaranta, cinquanta …).
numbers.it.why.compound: **{n}** → **{tens}** + **{ones}** = **{word}**: the tens first ({t} + {o}), in one word.
numbers.it.why.dropped: **{n}** → **{word}**: before {ones} the tens lose their last vowel ({tens} + {ones}).
numbers.it.why.accent: **{n}** → **{word}**: tre at the end of a longer number takes an accent: é.
numbers.it.why.big: **{n}** → **{word}**: Italian writes a number all in one word.
numbers.it.why.order: Italian says the tens first: **{word}** is {t} + {o} (**{tens}**-**{ones}**), not *{wrong}*.
numbers.it.why.spacing: A number is all one word: **{word}**.
numbers.it.why.date: **{day}** → **{said}**: a date takes the plain number with il; only the first of the month is primo (il primo maggio).
numbers.it.why.hour: **{time}** → **{said}**: alle and the hour; one o'clock is all'una.
numbers.it.why.half: **{time}** → **{said}**: e mezza counts from the hour that is there, not towards {next}.
numbers.de.tip: The ones first, then und, then the tens, all in one word: sieben-und-zwanzig (7 + 20).
numbers.de.why.teen: **{n}** → **{word}**: -zehn makes 13 to 19; sechzehn and siebzehn drop letters of sechs and sieben.
numbers.de.why.tens: **{n}** → **{word}**: -zig makes the tens; 30 is dreißig, with ß, and sechzig, siebzig drop letters.
numbers.de.why.ein: **{n}** → **{word}**: in a longer number 1 is ein, not eins (ein + und + {tens}).
numbers.de.why.compound: **{n}** → **{ones}** + **und** + **{tens}** = **{word}**: the ones first ({o} + {t}), joined by und, in one word.
numbers.de.why.big: **{n}** → **{word}**: German writes a number all in one word; hundert and tausend may also be einhundert and eintausend.
numbers.de.why.order: German says the ones first: **{word}** is {o} + {t} (**{ones}**-**und**-**{tens}**), not *{wrong}*.
numbers.de.why.spacing: A number is all one word: **{word}**.
numbers.de.why.date: **{day}.** {month} → **der {ordinal}** {month}: a date's day is the ordinal, with -te up to 19 and -ste from 20; erste, dritte, siebte and achte are special.
numbers.de.why.hour: **{time}** → **{said}**: um and the hour, with or without Uhr; one o'clock is um eins or um ein Uhr.
numbers.de.why.half: **{time}** → **{said}**: halb counts towards the next hour (halb + {next}); English half past and Italian e mezza count from the hour that is there.

cases.de.tip: **Ask the question.** The question in the word's place finds the case: *mit wem?* → **mit dem Hund**: the dative. The article mostly shows the case (der, den, dem, des). numbers.en.tip: The tens first, then the ones, with a hyphen: twenty-seven (20 + 7). After the hundreds, British English says and: one hundred and five.
numbers.en.why.forty: **{n}** → **{word}**: forty has no u, though four and fourteen have one.
numbers.en.why.eleven: **{n}** → **{word}**: eleven and twelve are words of their own; -teen begins at 13.
numbers.en.why.teen: **{n}** → **{word}**: 13 to 19 end in -teen (thirteen, fifteen, eighteen with one t).
numbers.en.why.tens: **{n}** → **{word}**: the tens end in -ty (twenty, thirty, forty, fifty).
numbers.en.why.compound: **{n}** → **{tens}** + **{ones}** = **{word}**: the tens first ({t} + {o}), joined by a hyphen.
numbers.en.why.hundred: **{n}** → **{word}**: hundred without -s, and British English says and before the rest.
numbers.en.why.big: **{n}** → **{word}**: thousand without -s, and before the last part under a hundred; a year is also said in pairs (twenty twenty-six).
numbers.en.why.order: English says the tens first: **{word}** is {t} + {o} (**{tens}**-**{ones}**), not *{wrong}*.
numbers.en.why.spacing: The tens and the ones are joined by a hyphen, the rest are words apart: **{word}**.
numbers.en.why.date: **{day}** → **{said}**: a date takes the ordinal; first, second, third, fifth, eighth, ninth and twelfth are their own, the rest add -th (twentieth).
numbers.en.why.hour: **{time}** → **{said}**: at and the hour; o'clock may follow.
numbers.en.why.half: **{time}** → **{said}**: half past counts from the hour that is there (in speech also {short}), not towards {next}.
